businessModel: Bundled with Apple hardware; search default revenue share (notably Google); Private Relay via iCloud+
updateCadence: Major version yearly with OS releases (September); point releases every ~4-8 weeks; STP roughly every 2 weeks
summary: Apple's WebKit browser for macOS, iOS, iPadOS and visionOS: best battery life, Advanced Fingerprinting Protection and iCloud Passwords/passkeys, but few customisation options and a limited extension model.
bestFor: Apple device users who want efficiency and battery life
People who want iCloud Passwords and passkeys everywhere
Users who want privacy protections without setup
iPhone/iPad users (WebKit is the only engine there)
notFor: Windows, Linux or Android users (not available)
People who want full ad blockers or power-user customisation
Developers who want Chrome-level DevTools breadth

pros.title: Battery and efficiency
pros.detail: Best-in-class energy use on Apple silicon Macs and iPhones.

pros.title: Anti-tracking by default
pros.detail: Intelligent Tracking Prevention blocks cross-site tracking; Advanced Fingerprinting Protection hardens against fingerprinting.

pros.title: iCloud Passwords and passkeys
pros.detail: Passwords app with passkeys, autofill and 2FA codes synced end-to-end encrypted.

pros.title: Fast WebKit
pros.detail: JavaScriptCore and WebKit trade top benchmark spots with Chrome.

pros.title: Apple Intelligence touches
pros.detail: Safari 27 adds AI tab organization, Notify Me page monitoring and AI-assisted Safari extension creation on supported devices.

cons.title: Apple only
cons.detail: No Windows, Linux or Android version (the Windows build was abandoned in 2012).

cons.title: Limited customisation
cons.detail: Little control over UI, search engines (fixed list), shortcuts and flags.

cons.title: Restrictive extensions
cons.detail: Web extensions are supported but blocking power is limited and distribution is via the App Store.

cons.title: Slower feature and security cadence
cons.detail: Major features arrive once a year, and older OS versions get Safari updates later.

signatureFeatures: Profiles and tab groups synced via iCloud
Apple Intelligence tab organization and Notify Me

faq.a: No. Safari 27.0 shipped stable on September 14, 2026 with macOS 27 Golden Gate and iOS 27; Safari 26.x continues for older macOS versions.

faq.q: Can I run Safari on Windows or Android?
faq.a: No. Safari is available only on macOS, iOS, iPadOS and visionOS; the Windows version ended in 2012.
No. Safari supports content blockers and web extensions through the App Store, but not full uBlock Origin.

devTools: Web Inspector solid, narrower than Chrome
longevity: Apple-backed, tied to every Apple OS
ai: Apple Intelligence, no chat or agent
